ui_bugs.issue: dept-assign-btn does not fire onClick when driven by Playwright page.click(force=true) — 0 POST /api/depts/assign-multi requests are emitted. Native element.click() (JS synthetic event) works and creates the assignments correctly. Root cause: some ancestor is likely intercepting mousedown/pointerdown (e.g. touch-preventing / drag-cancel handler or floating avatar overlay) so the composite mouse-event path is swallowed while the click-event path is not. In a real touch/tap scenario this may still work, but the divergence between synthetic-click and mouse-click flow is unusual for a plain <button> and warrants inspection.

rca of the issue: dept-assign-btn: page.click(force=true) dispatches mousedown→mouseup→click. Some ancestor (very likely the floating BakoMix ambient avatar / a global pointer capture) is consuming the mousedown or capturing the pointer BEFORE it reaches the button, so React's onClick synthetic event never fires. A synthetic element.click() bypasses the mouse-event path and dispatches only the click event, which does bubble to React's delegated root and fires assign(). Real user taps on modern browsers typically fire pointerdown+mousedown+click; if a global handler exists with stopImmediatePropagation on pointerdown, real users could also be affected. Recommend audit of window/document-level pointerdown/mousedown listeners in App.js or ambient-bako components. Missing success toast is likely because Sonner Toaster is not mounted inside the master console layout (needs verification).
